questions.q: What infrastructure does DPO remove compared to PPO-based RLHF?
options: DPO still requires a separate reward model and rollout loop, identical to PPO
A separate reward model to train and host, the rollout/generation loop during training, the value head, and advantage estimation
DPO removes the need for any preference data at all
DPO removes the SFT stage entirely
questions.explain: DPO trains like ordinary supervised fine-tuning directly on preference pairs, with no separate reward model, no generation loop, no value head, and no advantage estimation.

questions.q: What is the central tradeoff between DPO (offline) and PPO-based RLHF (online)?
options: There is no meaningful difference between offline and online training

DPO trains on a fixed preference dataset with no new samples generated, while PPO's policy generates fresh completions during training that get scored and used immediately, enabling exploration beyond the static dataset
Offline training is always faster regardless of dataset size
Online training never requires a reward model
questions.explain: PPO-based RLHF is online — it can score and learn from completions the policy generates that look nothing like the original preference data — while DPO can only push toward or away from responses already present in its fixed dataset.

questions.q: Why is PPO-based RLHF's online generation a double-edged sword according to this lesson?
options: It has no downsides at all compared to DPO
It gives PPO room to discover improvements beyond the static preference set, but also exposes it more to reward hacking by letting it exploit reward model blind spots anywhere in the generation space
Online generation makes PPO immune to reward hacking entirely
It only affects training speed, not quality or risk
questions.explain: The same online exploration that lets PPO improve beyond the fixed dataset also means it can wander into reward model blind spots that a purely offline method like DPO never visits.

questions.q: What do published empirical comparisons between DPO and PPO-based RLHF actually show, according to this lesson?
options: DPO is always strictly superior in every published comparison with no exceptions

The original DPO paper reported matching or exceeding PPO-based RLHF on some tasks with less infrastructure, but later work shows carefully tuned PPO can outperform DPO on some benchmarks — the comparison is sensitive to implementation quality on both sides
PPO-based RLHF has never been shown to outperform DPO under any circumstances
No empirical comparisons between the two methods have ever been published
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that neither method is strictly better — results depend heavily on how carefully each pipeline (reward modeling, KL control for PPO; training setup for DPO) is implemented.

questions.q: Why don't lesson 40's reward model evaluation diagnostics (held-out accuracy, calibration) directly apply to DPO's implicit reward?
options: Because DPO's implicit reward is never evaluated as a standalone scoring network the way an explicit reward model is — it's defined entirely from the policy's own log-probabilities, not a separate model
Because DPO doesn't use preference data at all
Because lesson 40's diagnostics apply equally well to DPO without any changes
Because DPO is trained before any preference data is collected
questions.explain: DPO has no separate reward model artifact to hold out and evaluate the way Chapter 6's reward model is — its implicit reward only exists as a function of the policy itself.
